"Near 100%" confidence that no agent silently reads users' mail (dump item 6) — the question Rob called the important one.** He named the class precisely: *"not automatically having an agent run and scrape our users' emails for anything useful, like a transcript or otherwise."* A prose promise cannot answer this (CR-3); the answer has to be a property of the code. | **DoD:** every automated agent's read scope enumerated **in code**, least-privilege credentials per source, an audit trail row written for each read, and a guard that **fails** when an automation reads a mailbox without an explicit per-source allowlist entry — with the guard's failure path driven live, not argued (the `guard:pii` / `check:env` pattern from Q71: an unfired guard is an untested one). An allowlist that defaults to *permitted* answers nothing. **The measured answer today: exactly ONE automation reads mail** — `n8n-gmail-capture`, mailbox `mbx-aivoicetech-rob`, credential `N8N_EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (unset ⇒ 503, so revocation is one env var, not a code change), audit stamp `activities.source='n8n'`, reading headers/subject/date/messageId/snippet only.
